To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
population-specific normative information is needed for the evaluation of physicians and that the data provided here are a first step in the process of providing such data.
the mean level of neurocognitive functioning for practicing physicians is lower than the general population and the standard deviation for physicians is higher than the general population.

(a) population specific normative data is necessary when evaluating physicians for fitness to practice; (b) population specific norm data is available for physicians; (c) population specific norm scores for physicians should be used in the fitness to practice evaluations of physicians.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most appropriate normative data for use in the evaluation of physicians.
the assessment and treatment of physicians who are underperforming or who are at risk of underperforming.
the identification of a population of physicians who are impaired by substance abuse, mental illness, or other conditions that affect their ability to practice medicine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of population norms is not appropriate for physician evaluations.
the data presented in this article should not be used for clinical practice.
the use of general population norms in neuropsychological assessment of practicing physicians may result in under-identification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data from the two physician studies were significantly different from the general population data, but not from each other.

physicians have a different pattern of performance on neuropsychological measures than the general population and that these differences are important when evaluating the cognitive abilities of physicians.
population-specific norms are required when evaluating physicians.
The main takeaway from our work is that
physicians should use physician-specific norms to interpret their test results.
physicians should use population specific normative data when evaluating the neurocognitive functioning of their peers.
the norms we developed for physicians are lower than those from general population samples.
